subject: Next steps & MAP — Atlas Health pilot decision timeline
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@atlashealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@atlashealth.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed MAP template

Hi Elena and Tom,

Great speaking with you both this morning — thanks for the time. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can keep momentum toward the pilot decision.

What I heard (confirm/correct):
- Goal: 8-week pilot to validate cost/safety/latency for patient-facing summarization workflows.
- Success criteria: 90th percentile latency < 350ms, acceptable hallucination rate on our eval set, and integration with SSO+audit logs.
- Timeline: decision by end of Q2 (you mentioned internal budgeting + procurement cadence).

Open items I want to action:
1) Stakeholder map — who’s the economic buyer and who will sign procurement? Please confirm names/roles.
2) Security/compliance needs — Elena, you mentioned a short SOC2 checklist and sample data requirements. If you can share the checklist, we’ll assemble the docs and a draft network diagram.
3) Technical scoping — propose a 60-min tech session with Marcus (copied) to walk integration and sample dataset needs.

I’ve attached a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) template and a proposed timeline to align milestones (kickoff, tech review, pilot start, procurement redline). If that looks good I’ll update dates once you confirm stakeholders and procurement owner.

Proposed next meeting: Tue 2026-03-24 10:00 AM PT — tech scoping + MAP review (Marcus to join).

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0183

Attachments: Proposed_MAP_Atlas_v1.docx (MAP template and suggested milestones)

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the succinct recap. Quick confirmations and a couple requests from our side:

Confirmations:
- Champion: Elena Martinez (Clinical AI Program Lead) — will drive clinical validation and acceptance tests.
- Economic buyer: Tom Reynolds (VP Finance) — final sign-off on budget.
- Procurement contact: procurement@atlashealth.com (cc’d) — handles contract and SOW.

Security/compliance: I attached our high-level Security & Privacy checklist (Atlas_Security_QA.pdf). Highlights:
- Must have SOC2 or equivalent evidence for hosted options.
- Data residency: pilot uses de-identified samples; production will require VPC/Private deployment discussion.
- Audit logging and key rotation processes need to be documented.

Timing: Budget approval meeting is tentatively scheduled for 2026-05-18. If we can get a draft commercial term sheet + MAP milestones by 2026-03-30, I can push to include Redwood in the procurement packet.

Elena

Hi all — quick technical notes following Rishi’s updates and the Atlas security checklist: 

1) Sample data: de-identified CSVs with columns (note_id, note_text, deid_token) are fine for an initial pilot. If possible, include a small validation set (~500 records) and an eval set (~200 records) flagged for hallucination checks.
2) Integration: we support HTTPS REST endpoints with API keys or token-based OIDC; for pilot, API key over TLS is acceptable. For production we’ll recommend mutual TLS or VPC option per Elena’s note.
3) Milestones (I added to SOW_Technical_Milestones.xlsx):
   - Tech kickoff + dataset handoff (week 0)
   - Integration & sandbox testing (weeks 1–2)
   - Eval runs + quality review (weeks 3–4)
   - Pilot tuning & acceptance (weeks 5–8)

Please confirm dataset delivery method and who on Atlas will drop the sample files. Also, if there are any specific retention policies we should know about, flag them now so we can include in the SOW.

- Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

Attachments: SOW_Technical_Milestones.xlsx
